findings.title: Member list is rendered with an invalid each helper
findings.body: The new member-list block is written as `{{each member in members itemView='group-member'}}` without the leading `#` and there is no closing `{{/each}}`. Handlebars treats this as an inline helper, not a block, so the group-member template is never rendered; the admin group member list and its remove links are missing or rendering fails. Use `{{#each member in members itemView='group-member'}} ... {{/each}}`.

findings.title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit
findings.body: `totalPages` computes `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (for example 50 members with limit 50), it reports 2 pages instead of 1. `showingLast` is then false and the Next action sets offset to user_count, so the admin UI goes to an empty page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (returning 0 when user_count is 0).

findings.title: Removing the last member on the last page leaves an empty member list
findings.body: `findMembers` clamps the requested offset with `Math.min(user_count, ...)`. If an admin removes the only member on the last page, user_count falls to the current offset (for example 50), so the reload requests offset=50 against a 50-member total and receives an empty array. The member list goes blank; clamp to the last valid page start or step back a page when offset >= user_count.

findings.title: Public group members endpoint now silently truncates at 50 with no public pagination
findings.body: The endpoint now defaults to limit 50, but the public group/members route and template have no pagination or load-more control. Public group pages therefore silently show only the first 50 members; before this change manual groups returned all members and automatic groups up to 200. Add pagination to the public page or avoid applying the 50-row default there. The supplied limit is also not capped, so callers can request arbitrarily large pages.

findings.title: Member reload uses the unsaved editable group name
findings.body: `findMembers` builds the URL from `this.get('name')`, but the admin form edits `name` directly. If an admin renames a group and then adds/removes a member or pages before saving, the add/remove request uses the id and succeeds, but the follow-up GET uses the unsaved new name and fails or returns 404, leaving the member list stale. Use the group id for admin member listing or the persisted name.

findings.title: Remove link is shown for automatic groups because automatic is read from the wrong context
findings.body: This template is the itemView for each member, so its context is the member rather than the parent group. `automatic` is a group attribute and is undefined in this scope, making `unless automatic` true; the remove link is shown even for automatic groups. Removing then fails with a 422. Pass the group's automatic flag into the item view or render the link conditionally from the parent template.

findings.title: Creating a group ignores the submitted alias_level
findings.body: `create` only assigns name and visible. `Group#asJSON` includes alias_level, and the form allows choosing it for a new group, so the submitted alias_level is silently ignored and the new group keeps the default until an explicit update. Assign alias_level in create (with the same presence check used in update).
